checks: Verified the byte digests and read the declared parts of 6b20e938071f0379 §§1–2, 4–5 and cde78a6346699a8a §§1 and 4. The frozen proof retains the common-cap hypotheses and reproduces the two boundary gains and the radical optimization directly.

The ordinary three-cap bound on A and K gives a≤w+v+u/4 and k≤9Q/4−F, with the smallest K cap Q−w because each ambient cap has common mass Q and zero B capture. The budget inequality gives k≤a+b−2F and Q≤4(a+b−F)/9. Combining b≤a+k with the former yields a≥F, hence r≥1/4. Substituting Q=q+w and a=u+v+rw gives (1).

The shifted cover at thresholds (−1,−1,2) gives τ≥δ+3 min(u,τ)/4. The alternative τ<u implies τ≥4δ≥w≥u. The proper original cut supplies an anchor on level −1 and positive u,w. Positivity of τ forces h>2. The factor 3/H maps the original cap into its strip between −1 and 2, with area 9w/H² and overlap with τ only on the null level-2 line. Thus 1/4≤r<θ≤1−9/H²<1.

The segment joins actual extrema of t on A and has constant transverse coordinate after a determinant-one shear in absolute value. A section of E+B is the interval [t₀+L,h+U] at the translated transverse coordinate. Since t₀<−1, h>2, and −2≤L≤U≤1, it strictly straddles zero. Expanding the displayed pointwise identity gives nonnegative terms, and Fubini gives Hb/3. Scaling by one half preserves the t≥0 cut and divides area by four. Then (1) implies 0<(5/2−r)w≤b(1−3H/16), giving H<16/3 and θ<1−(9/16)²=175/256.

Translating A transversely and K by half that displacement preserves the tested cut and midpoint compatibility. At height t+t₊ with t∈[2,h], the rightmost B point occurs in the E+B section, so the right boundary there is s₊ and the A+B boundary is at least s₊+a₊(t). The leftmost B point gives the separate left gain −a₋(t). Both shifts stay in t≥0. The two nonnegative gains sum to the width increase at any common height, including overlapping integration intervals, and their integrals add at least τ. This proves (4) using the same bodies throughout.

The interpolation of the lower A caps at −1 and h with weight 3/H lies in the cap at 2. Its positive endpoint areas are a−w and a. Since the latter cap at 2 has area a−τ, Brunn–Minkowski and division by √w give H≥J with a positive denominator from θ<1. Combining (1) and (4) gives Dw≤bN and N>0.

Differentiated the rationalized form J=3(Y+e)/((1−θ)(X+e)) independently and recovered both logarithmic derivatives. The limit as α decreases to 1 gives J≥3/√(1−θ); for α≥5/4 and θ≥1/4, 3α+θ≥4 ensures e/Y≥1/2 and J_θ≥J. The inequality θ≥3(α−1)/4+r/4 follows from v/w≤1.

Lowering θ to θ₀ and then lowering r to 1/4 stays in the region with N>0 and θ₀<1. At the two pieces of θ₀ the derivative signs are −3J_θD+7N and −3J_θD+55N. Checked D≥33/16, the first margin 297/32>7, and the second margin (33/2)J−55≥33√3−55>0. The quotient agrees across the piece boundary.

Independent Fraction arithmetic verifies the two low-α coefficients with D=153/64, the comparisons 961<972 and 6241<6300, and the large-α derivative upper bound 477/512−1215/1024=−261/1024. Direct substitution gives J(9/8,1/4)=1+√7. On the last branch J increases with α, so the relevant positive-N interval attaches to α=5/4. Every branch is strictly below 1/6.
